paragraphs: On Sunday, Dad drove Tom and Lily to Green Hill. Grandma and Grandpa were at home. Grandpa sat in front of the TV, and he did not say hello. "What is he watching?" asked Lily quietly. "Snowboarding," said Grandma with a smile. Lily looked at the screen. The room was quiet, and an old fan turned slowly. Everything was white, and a man talked very fast. "I have never seen real snow," said Lily.

Tom sat down next to Grandpa. He watched with his mouth open. "Is snowboarding similar to skateboarding?" he asked. Grandpa smiled, because he liked the question. "Yes, a little," said Grandpa, "but the board is bigger, and the hill is much higher." "I can skateboard, so I think that I can snowboard," said Tom. Grandma laughed. "In Green Hill it is hot, so you cannot try it here."

Lily sat on the floor and looked at the TV again. "Look, there is a red spot on the white hill!" she said. "That is a snowboarder," said Grandpa. The red spot came down the hill very fast. Then the snowboarder jumped into the air and landed on the snow. The man on TV said, "She is aged fifteen." "She is only two years older than Tom," said Lily. "And she is very brave!" "I am not scared," said Tom, "but I don't have a snowboard."

Soon Grandma came in with a big bowl of rice. "Lunch is ready!" she said. The rice smelled very good. "Can I watch the next race?" asked Grandpa. "No, you must eat with the children," said Grandma. "They came to see you, not the TV." Lily carried the plates to the table. "Thank you, my dear grandchild," said Grandma.

After lunch, Tom washed the plates, and Lily dried them. Then Grandpa asked, "Shall we continue watching?" "Yes, please!" said Lily and Tom. The next race was slower, but Lily watched every jump. Grandma sat next to them, and Grandpa put a cushion behind Lily's back. "One day, we will see real snow," said Grandpa. Lily smiled, because that was a nice idea.
